_comment: Hand-authored. Bank 5: the two inline jump tables, resolved at last, and the area-indexed structure pointer tables. See annotations/dispatch.json for the jump tables' registry entries.

regions.name: Inline jump table A (9 entries)
regions.description: Nine entries, each a handler address minus one, inline after the JSR at $9F2F - the $D6B0 convention, here through this bank's own copy at $9F10. The index is A, loaded from $51 two instructions earlier with NO mask and NO compare, so the caller gives no bound. THREE THINGS AGREE ON NINE. (1) Structural: entry 8 targets $9F44, and a tenth entry would reach $9F44, so the table cannot be longer without containing its own target. (2) The method is checked against a case where the code also answers: the sibling table at $A1C4 is bounded structurally at 10 and by its caller's CMP #$0A at 10, and they agree. (3) THE TRACE: seeding all nine and re-walking leaves this region as an unclaimed gap of exactly 18 bytes - 9 x 2 - with traced code on both sides and zero illegal opcodes. Entry 9 would be $8821, a plausible address rather than obvious garbage, so nothing here rules out a tenth entry that is simply never indexed.

regions.name: Inline jump table B (10 entries)
regions.description: Ten entries, each a handler address minus one, inline after the JSR at $A1C1. THE COUNT COMES FROM THE CALLER, which is what this project prefers: $A1A2 does LDA ($E4),Y / AND #$7F / SEC / SBC #$01 / STA $15 / CMP #$0A / BCC $A1B7, and the failing side takes an error path at $A1AA. So the index is 0 to 9 and can be nothing else. Two independent checks agree: entry 2 targets $A1D8, exactly where a tenth entry ends, and after seeding all ten the trace leaves this region as an unclaimed gap of exactly 20 bytes.

regions.name: Area to structure-set offset
regions.description: Nine bytes, values $16 and $18, read by $A78E as LDA $A7A7,Y with Y = $51, the area number. The value is used directly as a byte offset into the pointer table at $A7B0 ($A791 does TAY, then $A792 reads $A7B0,Y and $A7B1,Y), so it selects a pointer, not an index. Bounded structurally: $A7A7 + 9 is $A7B0, where the pointer table begins. NOT ESTABLISHED, and it matters: the game has more than nine areas, and nothing found so far stops $51 exceeding 8 on this path, which would read into the pointer table as if it were an offset. Only offsets $16 and $18 occur, and both select the same pointer, $AA8A.

regions.name: Structure pointers (35 entries)
regions.description: Thirty-five little-endian pointers, read by $A792/$A797 through the offset table above, and overlapped by a second view at $A7CA that $A79C reads with X fixed at $16. Bounded structurally: the lowest target above the table's own start is $A7F6, and a thirty-sixth entry would reach it. 21 distinct targets. THEY POINT AT STRUCTURE RECORDS - [next][dest][width][height][tiles] - which bank 5 $8155 blits into the 16 by 12 tile buffer at $0740, chaining through byte 0. 13 of the 21 targets start a chain; 48 links and 801 bytes come out of them, disjoint and colliding with nothing, and they are claimed one region per record by tools/parse-structs.py. CORRECTION to what this region said when it was first written: it said 'the pool is NOT partitioned' on the strength of chaining through byte 0 alone, which drifts. The rule that works is the record's own two size claims agreeing, next == 4 + width * height, and with it the chains stop on their own exactly where the pool ends. STILL NOT ESTABLISHED: the other eight targets, contiguous at $A8A6-$A938, whose first record fails that test. They are selected by table entries the area path never reaches - only offsets $16 and $18 occur there - so whatever reads them has not been found.
